CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

1. Region is Wonosobo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Wonosobo
4. Vice Regent is the Vice Regent of Wonosobo
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Wonosobo Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Apparatus of Wonosobo Regency tasked in the field of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children
7. Regional Apparatus Work Unit Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD is part of SKPD
8. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens in order to live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions.
9. Social welfare administration for women and children is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Government, Regional Government and society in the form of social services to meet the basic needs of every citizen, especially women and children, which includes social rehabilitation, social security, social empowerment, and social protection.
10. Social problems
11. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life.
12. Social empowerment is all efforts directed to make citizens experiencing social problems have power, so that they are able to meet their basic needs.
13. Social security is an institutionalized scheme to ensure all people can meet their basic needs for a decent life.
14. Social protection is all efforts directed to prevent and handle risks from social problems.
15. Special protection is
16. Social outreach is a series of activities to pick up women and children who are in parks, markets, streets and public places that can cause social problems, so that these women and children receive social welfare administration services.
17. Social organization is a social association formed by the community that is a legal entity or not a legal entity that functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare efforts.
18. Social Institution is an institution or work unit established by the community and or government that provides social welfare services
19. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (Twelve) years old including a child still in the womb.
20. Child in emergency situation is
21. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially.
22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and or mental obstacles so that their growth and development is disrupted properly.
23. Child welfare is a child's life that can guarantee their growth and development properly both physically, spiritually and socially.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
25. Poor family is a family that has no source of livelihood and does not have the ability to meet basic needs that are decent for humanity or people who have a source of livelihood but cannot meet decent basic needs.
26. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
27. Human trafficking is
28. Victim is
29. Person with disability is every person who has physical and or mental abnormalities that can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to perform properly consisting of persons with physical and mental disabilities
30. Social deviant is a person whose life does not conform to religious norms, moral norms, legal norms, and or community norms.
31. Care is various efforts given to children who do not have parents and are neglected, neglected children, and children experiencing behavioral problems, which are temporary in nature as a substitute for parents or family so that they can grow and develop properly both spiritually, physically, and socially.
32. Social assistance is assistance that is not permanent or temporary and is given within a certain period of time to social welfare beneficiaries who are unable so that they can improve their social welfare level and are able to carry out their social functions properly in community life both spiritually, physically, and socially.
33. Community members are residents of Wonosobo Regency and foreign citizens living in Wonosobo Regency.
34. Society is a group of community members who have interest and role in the field of social welfare.
35. Violence against children is

Article 18

1. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare from parents, family, the community, and the regional government to grow and develop normally.
2. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become good and useful members of society.
3. Every child has the right to receive maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development normally.
4. Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, mistreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and mental and social guidance.

Article 7

Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children c. improve the level of welfare, quality, and survival. d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence. e. increase community social resilience in preventing and handling social welfare problems.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world in the administration of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world and society.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

CHAPTER IX

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 39

1. Any person who neglects, commits acts of violence and/or exploitation against children as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 77 letter b, Article 80, Article 81, Article 82, and Article 88 of Law No. 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
2. Any person who employs children under working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

Article 19

1. Everyone is prohibited from neglecting, committing acts of violence and/or exploitation against children.
2. Everyone is prohibited from employing children under working age as regulated in the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER II

SCOPE

Article 2

The scope of social protection includes: women and children with social problems.

Part Two

Social Protection and Administration of Social Welfare for Women

Article 37

1. Social organizations and or the community may participate in conducting supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the laws and regulations

Article 14

Every Woman has the right to obtain social protection in the form of equal treatment and opportunity in education and training, employment, and protection of safety and/or health relating to women's reproductive function in accordance with norms of decent living and livelihood.

Article 35

1. The regional government shall supervise social protection and social welfare administration for women and children in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out with the principles of transparency and accountability.

Article 20

The regional government and/or the community can carry out social protection and the administration of social welfare for children for the purpose of improving child welfare, carried out in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 13

Technical implementation of social protection and the administration of social welfare for women and children as referred to in Article 8 paragraph (2) is further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Part Three

Social Protection and Administration of Social Welfare for Children

CHAPTER VI

COOPERATION

Article 29

1. The regional government may establish cooperation with other regional governments to carry out social protection and social welfare administration for women and children.
2. The form of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) may include:
a. repatriation and follow-up guidance;
b. social counseling
c. health services
d. provision of employment opportunities
e. education and training
f. research and development of science and technology
g. financing
h. procurement of facilities and infrastructure.
3. The procedures for cooperation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

CHAPTER VI

COOPERATION

Article 29

1. The regional government may establish cooperation with other regional governments to carry out social protection and social welfare administration for women and children.
2. The form of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) may include:
a. repatriation and follow-up guidance;
b. social counseling
c. health services
d. provision of employment opportunities
e. education and training
f. research and development of science and technology
g. financing
h. procurement of facilities and infrastructure.
3. The procedures for cooperation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 37

1. Social organizations and or the community may participate in conducting supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the laws and regulations

Article 18

1. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare from parents, family, the community, and the regional government to grow and develop normally.
2. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become good and useful members of society.
3. Every child has the right to receive maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development normally.
4. Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, mistreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and mental and social guidance.

Article 36

1. Functional supervision of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children shall be carried out by functional supervisory officials.
2. Technical operational supervision of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children organized by social organizations and the community shall be carried out by SKPD/UKPD.
3. Further provisions regarding the implementation of supervision shall be regulated by Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

DECIDES:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 8

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently Clear

Paragraph (3)

a. What is meant by preventive is efforts to prevent the emergence of complex social problems in society, which are directed both at individuals and community groups who are predicted to become sources of persons with social welfare problems.

b. What is meant by repressive is efforts in the form of supervision, with the aim of reducing and/or controlling the number of persons with social welfare problems directed at a person or group of persons with social welfare problems.

c. What is meant by rehabilitative is efforts of care, vocational training, accessibility and empowerment aimed at changing the mental attitude of persons with social welfare problems from a non-productive state to a productive state.

d. Sufficiently Clear;

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

1. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare from parents, family, the community, and the regional government to grow and develop normally.
2. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become good and useful members of society.
3. Every child has the right to receive maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development normally.
4. Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation to address social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

CHAPTER VI

COOPERATION

Article 29

1. The regional government may establish cooperation with other regional governments to carry out social protection and social welfare administration for women and children.
2. The form of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) may include:
a. repatriation and follow-up guidance;
b. social counseling
c. health services
d. provision of employment opportunities
e. education and training
f. research and development of science and technology
g. financing
h. procurement of facilities and infrastructure.
3. The procedures for cooperation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 7

Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children c. improve the level of welfare, quality, and survival. d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence. e. increase community social resilience in preventing and handling social welfare problems.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world in the administration of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world and society.

Article 8

Paragraph (1) In order to obtain optimal results, in the framework of program implementation it must be integrated and cross-sectoral with a comprehensive approach both between professions and between agencies by developing active participation from the community.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently Clear

Paragraph (3)

a. What is meant by preventive is efforts to prevent the emergence of complex social problems in society, which are directed both at individuals and community groups who are predicted to become sources of persons with social welfare problems.

b. What is meant by repressive is efforts in the form of supervision, with the aim of reducing and/or controlling the number of persons with social welfare problems directed at a person or group of persons with social welfare problems.

c. What is meant by rehabilitative is efforts of care, vocational training, accessibility and empowerment aimed at changing the mental attitude of persons with social welfare problems from a non-productive state to a productive state.

d. Sufficiently Clear;

Article 35

1. The regional government shall supervise social protection and social welfare administration for women and children in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out with the principles of transparency and accountability.

Article 18

1. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare from parents, family, the community, and the regional government to grow and develop normally.
2. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become good and useful members of society.
3. Every child has the right to receive maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development normally.
4. Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, mistreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and mental and social guidance.

Article 36

1. Functional supervision of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children shall be carried out by functional supervisory officials.
2. Technical operational supervision of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children organized by social organizations and the community shall be carried out by SKPD/UKPD.
3. Further provisions regarding the implementation of supervision shall be regulated by Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

Article 37

1. Social organizations and or the community may participate in conducting supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the laws and regulations

CHAPTER VIII

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 38

1. Every social organization that has obtained a permit in the implementation of social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children, which deliberately does not provide social services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (5), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
2. Every social organization that implements social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children without a permit as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (6), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of: a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. revocation of permit.

Article 17

Every institution, both government and private, that organizes public services or employs women must provide adequate facilities for the interests of women.

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

CHAPTER IX

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 39

1. Any person who neglects, commits acts of violence and/or exploitation against children as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 77 letter b, Article 80, Article 81, Article 82, and Article 88 of Law No. 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
2. Any person who employs children under working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

ADMINISTRATION

Part One

General

Article 23

1. In carrying out the responsibility as referred to in Article 21 paragraph (3), SKPD/UKPD shall prepare a plan for social protection and social welfare administration for women and children.
2. In preparing the plan as referred to in paragraph (2), it shall be guided by the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJM) and the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJP).
3. The social welfare administration plan as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 19

1. Everyone is prohibited from neglecting, committing acts of violence and/or exploitation against children.
2. Everyone is prohibited from employing children under working age as regulated in the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world in the administration of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world and society.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation to address social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 35

1. The regional government shall supervise social protection and social welfare administration for women and children in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out with the principles of transparency and accountability.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2012

CONCERNING

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation to address social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

e. education and training

3. The procedures for cooperation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

1. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare from parents, family, the community, and the regional government to grow and develop normally.
2. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become good and useful members of society.
3. Every child has the right to receive maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development normally.
4. Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, mistreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and mental and social guidance.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

1. Region is Wonosobo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Wonosobo
4. Vice Regent is the Vice Regent of Wonosobo
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Wonosobo Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Apparatus of Wonosobo Regency tasked in the field of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children
7. Regional Apparatus Work Unit Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD is part of SKPD
8. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens in order to live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions.
9. Social welfare administration for women and children is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Government, Regional Government and society in the form of social services to meet the basic needs of every citizen, especially women and children, which includes social rehabilitation, social security, social empowerment, and social protection.
10. Social problems
11. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life.
12. Social empowerment is all efforts directed to make citizens experiencing social problems have power, so that they are able to meet their basic needs.
13. Social security is an institutionalized scheme to ensure all people can meet their basic needs for a decent life.
14. Social protection is all efforts directed to prevent and handle risks from social problems.
15. Special protection is
16. Social outreach is a series of activities to pick up women and children who are in parks, markets, streets and public places that can cause social problems, so that these women and children receive social welfare administration services.
17. Social organization is a social association formed by the community that is a legal entity or not a legal entity that functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare efforts.
18. Social Institution is an institution or work unit established by the community and or government that provides social welfare services
19. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (Twelve) years old including a child still in the womb.
20. Child in emergency situation is
21. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially.
22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and or mental obstacles so that their growth and development is disrupted properly.
23. Child welfare is a child's life that can guarantee their growth and development properly both physically, spiritually and socially.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
25. Poor family is a family that has no source of livelihood and does not have the ability to meet basic needs that are decent for humanity or people who have a source of livelihood but cannot meet decent basic needs.
26. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
27. Human trafficking is
28. Victim is
29. Person with disability is every person who has physical and or mental abnormalities that can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to perform properly consisting of persons with physical and mental disabilities
30. Social deviant is a person whose life does not conform to religious norms, moral norms, legal norms, and or community norms.
31. Care is various efforts given to children who do not have parents and are neglected, neglected children, and children experiencing behavioral problems, which are temporary in nature as a substitute for parents or family so that they can grow and develop properly both spiritually, physically, and socially.
32. Social assistance is assistance that is not permanent or temporary and is given within a certain period of time to social welfare beneficiaries who are unable so that they can improve their social welfare level and are able to carry out their social functions properly in community life both spiritually, physically, and socially.
33. Community members are residents of Wonosobo Regency and foreign citizens living in Wonosobo Regency.
34. Society is a group of community members who have interest and role in the field of social welfare.
35. Violence against children is

Article 33

1. The provision of counseling, guidance, supervision, and consultation as referred to in Article 30 letter c shall cover planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.
2. Counseling and/or guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be directed to the community, social organizations and business entities.
3. The provision of counseling, guidance, supervision, and consultation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by SKPD/UKPD.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

CHAPTER VI

COOPERATION

Article 29

1. The regional government may establish cooperation with other regional governments to carry out social protection and social welfare administration for women and children.
2. The form of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) may include:
a. repatriation and follow-up guidance;
b. social counseling
c. health services
d. provision of employment opportunities
e. education and training
f. research and development of science and technology
g. financing
h. procurement of facilities and infrastructure.
3. The procedures for cooperation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 29

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (2) letter h.

What is meant by facilities and infrastructure in this regulation is all facilities funded and obtained from the Regional Budget and/or State Budget to support social welfare functions. Among others: Regional Hospitals, Shelters, Transit Houses, Social Transport Vehicles, Facilities at Nursing Homes, Orphanages, Foundations, etc.

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 14

Every Woman has the right to obtain social protection in the form of equal treatment and opportunity in education and training, employment, and protection of safety and/or health relating to women's reproductive function in accordance with norms of decent living and livelihood.

Article 7

Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children c. improve the level of welfare, quality, and survival. d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence. e. increase community social resilience in preventing and handling social welfare problems.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world in the administration of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world and society.

Article 15

Every woman is obliged to maintain her dignity and that of her family as well as her nature as a woman by taking into account her function and role in family and/or community life in accordance with her abilities.

Article 18

1. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare from parents, family, the community, and the regional government to grow and develop normally.
2. Every child has the right to receive social protection and the administration of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become good and useful members of society.
3. Every child has the right to receive maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development normally.
4. Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, mistreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and mental and social guidance.

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

Article 8

Paragraph (1) In order to obtain optimal results, in the framework of program implementation it must be integrated and cross-sectoral with a comprehensive approach both between professions and between agencies by developing active participation from the community.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently Clear

Paragraph (3)

a. What is meant by preventive is efforts to prevent the emergence of complex social problems in society, which are directed both at individuals and community groups who are predicted to become sources of persons with social welfare problems.

b. What is meant by repressive is efforts in the form of supervision, with the aim of reducing and/or controlling the number of persons with social welfare problems directed at a person or group of persons with social welfare problems.

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 31

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 19

1. Everyone is prohibited from neglecting, committing acts of violence and/or exploitation against children.
