Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2012

CONCERNING

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation to address social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18–59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation to address social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

The role of business entities as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) letter g in social protection and social welfare administration for women and children shall be carried out as part of social and environmental responsibility in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 42

All provisions relating to social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children that existed before the promulgation of this Regional Regulation, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

3. Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of: a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. revocation of permit.

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 7

Social protection for women and children aims to:

f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world in the administration of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world and society.

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 39

1. Any person who neglects, commits acts of violence and/or exploitation against children as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 77 letter b, Article 80, Article 81, Article 82, and Article 88 of Law No. 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
2. Any person who employs children under working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

Article 3

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0–18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

COOPERATION

d. provision of employment opportunities
e. education and training
f. research and development of science and technology
g. financing

Article 15

Every woman is obliged to maintain her dignity and that of her family as well as her nature as a woman by taking into account her function and role in family and/or community life in accordance with her abilities.

Article 26

The role of business entities as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) letter g in social protection and social welfare administration for women and children shall be carried out as part of social and environmental responsibility in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13

Technical implementation of social protection and the administration of social welfare for women and children as referred to in Article 8 paragraph (2) is further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 17

Every institution, both government and private, that organizes public services or employs women must provide adequate facilities for the interests of women.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation to address social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation to address social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0–18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled in a reasonable manner, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0–18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but who due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. A street child is a child aged 0–18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0–18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which may interfere with or constitute obstacles and impediments for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18–59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

h. OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2012

CONCERNING

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation to address social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 5

a. What is meant by “the principle of solidarity” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social concern to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by “the principle of justice” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination, and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by “the principle of benefit” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by “the principle of integration” is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by “the principle of partnership” is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, with the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government’s partner in addressing social welfare problems and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by “the principle of transparency” is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by “the principle of accountability” is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

h. What is meant by “the principle of participation” is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by “the principle of professionalism” is that every implementation of social welfare for the community should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of its duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by “the principle of sustainability” is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by “the principle of non-discrimination” is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by “gender equality” is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.
